chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from some of our companions, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

A man came to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام with another man and said, “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, this man has accused me of fornication.” He said to him, “Do you have evidence?” He said, “No, but make him swear an oath.” So Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said, “There is no oath in a hadd, and there is no qiṣāṣ concerning a bone.”

key_terms.عَظْمٍ: A bone; here referring to injury involving bone
key_terms.قَذَفَنِي: He accused me of fornication or slandered me with a charge entailing hadd
key_terms.يَمِينَ: An oath used in legal proceedings

ai.seo_question: Can an oath be used to establish a hadd punishment in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام regarding accusations that entail hadd punishment. He rejects establishing such a matter through an oath when there is no evidence, and he also states that qiṣāṣ does not apply in the case of a bone.
